note.fact: For R=Z_(p) and a field K of characteristic the prime p, the formula ρ(a/b)=ā b̄^(-1), using a representative with p∤b, defines a unital ring map. Its kernel is pR, and it identifies R/pR with the prime subfield Z/pZ of K.

grounds.reason: p is prime and K has characteristic p.
R consists of fractions admitting denominators not divisible by p.

note.justification: An integer has zero image in K exactly when divisible by p. Cross multiplication proves independence of representatives and the ring laws. Thus a/b has zero image exactly when p divides a, equivalently a/b∈pR. For p∤b, integers u,t with ub+tp=1 show that the residue of a/b equals the residue of the integer au. Hence every residue is an integer residue, and their kernel is pZ.

70: and the namespace `Submonoid.LocalizationMap`.
71: 
72: To reason about the localization as a quotient type, use `mk_eq_of_mk'` and associated lemmas.
73: These show the quotient map `mk : R → M → Localization M` equals the surjection
74: `LocalizationMap.mk'` induced by the map `algebraMap : R →+* Localization M`.
75: The lemma `mk_eq_of_mk'` hence gives you access to the results in the rest of the file,
76: which are about the `LocalizationMap.mk'` induced by any localization map.
77: 
78: The proof that "a `CommRing` `K` which is the localization of an integral domain `R` at `R \ {0}`
79: is a field" is a `def` rather than an `instance`, so if you want to reason about a field of
80: fractions `K`, assume `[Field K]` instead of just `[CommRing K]`.
81: 
82: ## Tags
83: localization, ring localization, commutative ring localization, characteristic predicate,
84: commutative ring, field of fractions
85: -/

87: @[expose] public section
88: 
89: assert_not_exists AlgHom Ideal
90: 
91: open Function
92: 
93: section CommSemiring
94: 
95: variable {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] (M : Submonoid R) (S : Type*) [CommSemiring S]
96: variable [Algebra R S] {P : Type*} [CommSemiring P]
97: 
98: /-- An auxiliary typeclass to avoid auto-generated declarations
99: under the `IsLocalization` namespace. -/
100: class IsLocalization' : Prop extends M.IsLocalizationMap (algebraMap R S)
101: 
102: /-- The typeclass `IsLocalization (M : Submonoid R) S` where `S` is an `R`-algebra
103: expresses that `S` is isomorphic to the localization of `R` at `M`. -/
104: abbrev IsLocalization := @IsLocalization'
105: 
106: theorem isLocalization_iff_isLocalizationMap :
107:     IsLocalization M S ↔ M.IsLocalizationMap (algebraMap R S) :=
108:   ⟨fun ⟨h⟩ ↦ h, fun h ↦ ⟨h⟩⟩
109: 
110: theorem isLocalization_iff : IsLocalization M S ↔
111:     (∀ y : M, IsUnit (algebraMap R S y)) ∧
112:     (∀ z : S, ∃ x : R × M, z * algebraMap R S x.2 = algebraMap R S x.1) ∧
113:     ∀ {x y : R}, algebraMap R S x = algebraMap R S y → ∃ c : M, c * x = c * y := by
114:   rw [isLocalization_iff_isLocalizationMap, Submonoid.isLocalizationMap_iff]
115: 
116: variable {M}
117: 
118: namespace IsLocalization
119: 
120: section IsLocalization
121: 
122: variable [IsLocalization M S]
123: 
124: section
125: 
126: /-- Everything in the image of `algebraMap` is a unit. -/
127: theorem map_units : ∀ y : M, IsUnit (algebraMap R S y) :=
128:   IsLocalization'.toIsLocalizationMap.map_units
129: 
130: variable (M) {S}
131: /-- Every element in the localization can be expressed as a quotient of an element in the
132: range of `algebraMap` by the image of an element of the submonoid. -/
133: theorem surj : ∀ z : S, ∃ x : R × M, z * algebraMap R S x.2 = algebraMap R S x.1 :=
134:   IsLocalization'.toIsLocalizationMap.surj
135: 
136: variable {M} in
137: theorem exists_of_eq {x y : R} : algebraMap R S x = algebraMap R S y → ∃ c : M, c * x = c * y :=
138:   IsLocalization'.toIsLocalizationMap.exists_of_eq
139: 
140: variable (S)
141: 
142: variable {M} in
143: theorem smul_bijective (m : M) : Bijective fun s : S ↦ m • s := by
144:   simpa only [Submonoid.smul_def, Algebra.smul_def] using! (map_units S m).smul_bijective
145: 
146: /-- `IsLocalization.toLocalizationMap M S` shows `S` is the monoid localization of `R` at `M`. -/
147: abbrev toLocalizationMap : M.LocalizationMap S where
148:   __ := algebraMap R S
149:   toFun := algebraMap R S
150:   isLocalizationMap := IsLocalization'.toIsLocalizationMap
151: 
152: @[simp]
153: lemma toLocalizationMap_toMonoidHom :
154:     (toLocalizationMap M S).toMonoidHom = (.ofClass (algebraMap R S) : R →*₀ S) := rfl
155: 
156: @[simp] lemma coe_toLocalizationMap : ⇑(toLocalizationMap M S) = algebraMap R S := rfl
157: 
158: lemma toLocalizationMap_apply (x) : toLocalizationMap M S x = algebraMap R S x := rfl
159: 
160: theorem surj₂ : ∀ z w : S, ∃ z' w' : R, ∃ d : M,
161:     (z * algebraMap R S d = algebraMap R S z') ∧ (w * algebraMap R S d = algebraMap R S w') :=
162:   (toLocalizationMap M S).surj₂
163: 
164: /-- The kernel of `algebraMap` is equal to the annihilator by `map_units'` -/
165: theorem eq_iff_exists {x y} : algebraMap R S x = algebraMap R S y ↔ ∃ c : M, ↑c * x = ↑c * y :=
166:   (toLocalizationMap M S).eq_iff_exists

299: /- This lemma characterizes the kernel of `TensorProduct.mapOfCompatibleSMul`. Together with
300: `TensorProduct.mapOfCompatibleSMul_surjective` it gives an alternative characterization of
301: `M ⊗[A] N` as the quotient of `M ⊗[R] N` by the submodule `S` described below. -/
302: lemma ker_mapOfCompatibleSMul :
303:     (mapOfCompatibleSMul A R A M N).ker =
304:       Submodule.span A {(a • m) ⊗ₜ[R] n - m ⊗ₜ[R] (a • n) | (a : A) (m : M) (n : N)} := by
305:   refine (Submodule.span_eq_of_le (mapOfCompatibleSMul A R A M N).ker ?_ ?_).symm
306:   · rintro - ⟨a, m, n, rfl⟩
307:     simp [smul_tmul]
308:   · let S := Submodule.span A {(a • m) ⊗ₜ[R] n - m ⊗ₜ[R] (a • n) | (a : A) (m : M) (n : N)}
309:     let F : M ⊗[A] N →ₗ[A] (M ⊗[R] N) ⧸ S := TensorProduct.lift ({
310:       toFun m := {
311:         toFun n := S.mkQ (m ⊗ₜ[R] n)
312:         map_add' _ _ := by simp [tmul_add]
313:         map_smul' a n := by
314:           rw [Submodule.mkQ_apply, Submodule.mkQ_apply, ← Submodule.Quotient.mk_smul, eq_comm,
315:             Submodule.Quotient.eq, RingHom.id_apply]
316:           exact Submodule.subset_span ⟨a, m, n, rfl⟩ }
317:       map_add' _ _ := by ext _; simp [add_tmul]
318:       map_smul' _ _ := by simp; rfl })
319:     have h : F ∘ₗ mapOfCompatibleSMul A R A M N = S.mkQ := by ext; simp [S, F]
320:     change (mapOfCompatibleSMul A R A M N).ker ≤ S
321:     rw [← Submodule.ker_mkQ S, ← h]
322:     exact (mapOfCompatibleSMul A R A M N).ker_le_ker_comp F

22: /-- The `ZMod n`-module structure on commutative monoids whose elements have order dividing `n ≠ 0`.
23: Also implies a group structure via `Module.addCommMonoidToAddCommGroup`.
24: See note [reducible non-instances]. -/
25: abbrev AddCommMonoid.zmodModule [NeZero n] [AddCommMonoid M] (h : ∀ (x : M), n • x = 0) :
26:     Module (ZMod n) M := by
27:   have h_mod (c : ℕ) (x : M) : (c % n) • x = c • x := by
28:     suffices (c % n + c / n * n) • x = c • x by rwa [add_nsmul, mul_nsmul, h, add_zero] at this
29:     rw [Nat.mod_add_div']
30:   have := NeZero.ne n
31:   match n with
32:   | n + 1 => exact {
33:     smul := fun (c : Fin _) x ↦ c.val • x
34:     smul_zero := fun _ ↦ nsmul_zero _
35:     zero_smul := fun _ ↦ zero_nsmul _
36:     smul_add := fun _ _ _ ↦ nsmul_add _ _ _
37:     one_smul := fun _ ↦ (h_mod _ _).trans <| one_nsmul _
38:     add_smul := fun _ _ _ ↦ (h_mod _ _).trans <| add_nsmul _ _ _
39:     mul_smul := fun _ _ _ ↦ (h_mod _ _).trans <| mul_nsmul' _ _ _
40:   }

44: abbrev AddCommGroup.zmodModule {G : Type*} [AddCommGroup G] (h : ∀ (x : G), n • x = 0) :
45:     Module (ZMod n) G :=
46:   match n with
47:   | 0 => AddCommGroup.toIntModule G
48:   | _ + 1 => AddCommMonoid.zmodModule h

402: def assoc : (M ⊗[A] P) ⊗[R] Q ≃ₗ[B] M ⊗[A] (P ⊗[R] Q) :=
403:   LinearEquiv.ofLinear
404:     (lift <| lift <| lcurry R A B P Q _ ∘ₗ mk A B M (P ⊗[R] Q))
405:     (lift <| uncurry R A B P Q _ ∘ₗ curry (mk R B _ Q))

407:     (by ext; rfl)

412: theorem assoc_tmul (m : M) (p : P) (q : Q) :
413:     assoc R A B M P Q ((m ⊗ₜ p) ⊗ₜ q) = m ⊗ₜ (p ⊗ₜ q) :=

417: theorem assoc_symm_tmul (m : M) (p : P) (q : Q) :

434: /-- `B`-linear equivalence between `M ⊗[A] (A ⊗[R] N)` and `M ⊗[R] N`.
435: In particular useful with `B = A`. -/
436: def cancelBaseChange : M ⊗[A] (A ⊗[R] N) ≃ₗ[B] M ⊗[R] N :=
437:   letI g : (M ⊗[A] A) ⊗[R] N ≃ₗ[B] M ⊗[R] N := congr (AlgebraTensorModule.rid A B M) (.refl R N)

440: /-- Base change distributes over tensor product. -/
441: def distribBaseChange : A ⊗[R] (N ⊗[R] Q) ≃ₗ[A] (A ⊗[R] N) ⊗[A] (A ⊗[R] Q) :=
442:   (cancelBaseChange _ _ _ _ _ ≪≫ₗ assoc _ _ _ _ _ _).symm

446: @[simp]
447: theorem cancelBaseChange_tmul (m : M) (n : N) (a : A) :
448:     cancelBaseChange R A B M N (m ⊗ₜ (a ⊗ₜ n)) = (a • m) ⊗ₜ n :=

452: theorem cancelBaseChange_symm_tmul (m : M) (n : N) :

arguments.statement: ∃ S : Submonoid ℤ, (∀ b : ℤ, b ∈ S ↔ ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b) ∧ IsLocalization S (R p)
arguments.proof:
classical
have hp : Prime (p : ℤ) := Nat.prime_iff_prime_int.mp h_H001.1
let S : Submonoid ℤ :=
  { carrier := {b | ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b}
    one_mem' := hp.not_dvd_one
    mul_mem' := fun ha hb h => (hp.dvd_mul.mp h).elim ha hb }
refine ⟨S, fun b => Iff.rfl, ?_⟩
rw [isLocalization_iff]
have hc : RingCarrier p := h_T006.1.1
have bn : ∀ b : S, (b.val : ℚ) ≠ 0 := by
  intro b hb
  have : b.val = 0 := by exact_mod_cast hb
  exact b.property (this ▸ dvd_zero _)
refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
· intro b
  let t : R p := ⟨(1 : ℚ) / b.val, (hc _).2 ⟨1, b.val, b.property, by simp⟩⟩
  apply isUnit_iff_exists_inv.mpr
  refine ⟨t, ?_⟩
  apply Subtype.ext
  change (b.val : ℚ) * (1 / b.val) = 1
  field_simp
· intro z
  obtain ⟨a,b,hb,he⟩ := (hc z.val).1 z.property
  refine ⟨(a, ⟨b,hb⟩), ?_⟩
  apply Subtype.ext
  change z.val * (b : ℚ) = (a : ℚ)
  rw [he]
  exact div_mul_cancel₀ _ (bn ⟨b,hb⟩)
· intro a b hab

intro s hs hsur hc
letI : CharP K p := hc

simp [eta,he]
